title: Bynario AI identifies Caddy php_fastcgi authorization bypass
summary: When an index.php file is absent, Caddy's php_fastcgi fallback can fail to rewrite a dot-segment request. Path matchers authorize the cleaned path while the FastCGI transport executes a script named by the raw path, allowing access-control rules to be bypassed.
ai_role: The Caddy maintainer advisory explicitly says Bynario AI identified and validated the issue; the technical report was partly AI-written and manually reviewed. The advisory was published 2026-11-04, the known public AI-attribution date. The private discovery/report date and model version are not stated.
classification_note: The maintainer advisory discloses the issue and patch. It does not claim exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Fixed in Caddy v2.11.8. The authorization bypass applies to configurations where php_fastcgi's rewrite route does not run, including the documented default when index.php is absent; the advisory describes additional configuration prerequisites for RCE escalation.

impacts.conditions: Requires an affected php_fastcgi route configuration (for example, no index.php candidate or index disabled) and a known existing .php file. A remote unauthenticated request with cleaned-path mismatch bypasses authorization; with an attacker-controlled PHP file, the advisory demonstrated remote code execution. Sites with an index.php/front controller are masked.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory reports a demonstrated reproduction; it does not establish exploitation in the wild.
